drafts.question: How many people in Sokoto State were affected by floods in October 2024?
drafts.restatement: How many people in Sokoto State were affected by floods in October 2024?
drafts.name: Sokoto State
drafts.text:
*Flooding: Sokoto State* — experimental

In 2024, radar saw about 4,120 ha of Sokoto State under water on its biggest pass (27 August 2024), and 26,000 ha at some point in the season (18,590 ha on farmland, 4,880 ha in the river floodplain, 2,540 ha on other land).

Satellite radar saw floodwater in Sokoto State in every rainy season 2015–2026 (12 seasons). The largest was in 2020: about 22,210 ha on its biggest pass (17 September 2020), and 58,430 ha under water at some point that season (41,290 ha on farmland, 10,320 ha in the river floodplain, 6,820 ha on other land).

In 2024, radar passes saw 26,000 ha under water at some point; UNOSAT's event map of 5–9 September 2024 and 9–13 November 2024, built from several days and sensors, shows 123,410 ha. UNOSAT's map covers several days, so it catches more of the flood than single passes.

Radar can't judge 35% of Sokoto State (about 1,144,280 ha: built-up land, dense trees and dry sandy ground, where radar can't tell water from land), so floods there aren't counted. It can't see water between buildings: for built-up parts, flood reports are the source.

The river floodplain: water covered 47,650 ha of Sokoto State in some years between 1984 and 2020, and 21,640 ha in half the years or more (JRC Global Surface Water). Water there is partly the river's normal rise.

Kasafi's own radar check (Sentinel-1, normally dry farmland only) found floodwater in 2017, 2020, 2024; the most in 2020 (1.7% of that farmland).

Across the 23 LGAs of Sokoto State, the 2024 share of land under floodwater (radar) ranged from 0.0% (Sokoto South) to 8.5% (Sokoto North); the median was 0.6%. Most land under water: Sokoto North (8.5%), Kebbe (2.4%), Tambuwal (2.2%). Least: Sokoto South (0.0%), Dange Shuni (0.1%), Isa (0.2%).

*Ranking (23 LGAs)*
Highest:
1. Sokoto North: 8.5% (24 obs)
2. Kebbe: 2.4% (13 obs)
3. Tambuwal: 2.2% (13 obs)
4. Goronyo: 1.6% (11 obs)
5. Kware: 1.4% (11 obs)
Lowest:
19. Shagari: 0.2% (24 obs)
20. Gudu: 0.2% (13 obs)
21. Isa: 0.2% (11 obs)
22. Dange Shuni: 0.1% (11 obs)
23. Sokoto South: 0.0% (11 obs)

The map shows each LGA's share of land under water at some point in 2024.

Budget lines are linked per LGA: ask about one LGA to see its lines.

Kasafi reports what the satellite record shows; it makes no judgement of causes or of anyone's work. This is information only, not an official flood warning.

Sources: Copernicus Global Flood Monitoring (Contains modified Copernicus Emergency Management Service information [2015–2026]); UNOSAT satellite-detected water extents (HDX); JRC Global Surface Water; Copernicus Sentinel-1 RTC (Kasafi's check); boundaries GRID3 wards and OCHA COD-AB LGAs.
